High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Case :- Application U/S 528 Bnss No. - 16330 of 2025

Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Vijay Kumar Mishra
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Arun Kumar Singh Deshwal,J.
1.

Heard Sri Vijay Kr. Mishra, learned counsel for the applicants and Pankaj Saxena, learned A.G.A.
for the State.
2. Learned counsel for the applicants is permitted to correct the prayer clause.

3. The instant application has been filed to quash the summoning order date 18.3.2025, charge sheet dated 11.2.2025 and all subsequent proceeding of case No. 14731 of 2025, case crime No. 85 of 2024,
under Section 498A, 323, 504, 506 354, 313, 377 IPC and 3/4 D.P. Act, P.S. Chetganj, District Varanasi.

4. Learned counsel for the applicants submits that the dispute between the parties is matrimonial in nature and considering this fact, the Court by order dated 12.9.2024 in Criminal Writ Petition No.
13303 of 2024, referred this matter before the mediation centre.

In pursuance of the said order, the Rajat Nigam And 6 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 9 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176950217/
1 parties appeared before the mediation centre and entered into a settlement agreement dated 10.12.2024.

sentences.text: 5. It is further submitted by learned counsel for the applicants that in pursuance of the above settlement agreement, the parties have also filed an application under Section 13-B Hindu Marriage Act.

Additionally, in compliance of the settlement agreement, the applicants have already paid Rs.
13 Lakh at the time of filing the application u/s 13-B Hindu Marriage Act and remaining Rs.7 Lakh will be paid at the time of final order to be passed under Section 13-B Hindu Marriage Act.

6. Considering the submission of the counsel for the parties and on perusal of the record it is clear that the parties have settled their dispute and entered into a settlement agreement dated 10.12.2024.
In such circumstances, continuation of impugned proceeding will amount to travesty of justice.

7. Thus, in view of the well settled principles of law as laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2003(4) SCC 675 (B.S. Joshi Vs. State of Haryana), J.T. 2008(9) SC 192 (Nikhil Merchant Vs.
Central Bureau of investigation and another), (2012) 10 SCC 303 (Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab),
(2014) 9 SCC 653 (Yogendra Yadav and others Vs. State of Jharkhand) and also (2014) 6 SCC 466 (Narendra Singh Vs. State of Punjab), and in view of the settlement agreement dated 10.12.2024 before the mediation centre, the proceeding of the aforesaid case is hereby quashed.
8.
